docs.title: Shape-adaptive robust regression
docs.text:

Python estimators for regression under skewness and heavy tails, developed for the Arashi–Yüzbaşı study From Residual-Moment Penalties to Shape-Adaptive Robust Estimation under Skewness and Heavy Tails.

docs.title: Clear boundaries
docs.text:
Version 0.1.0 provides the installable estimator API and a small installation test. This is a GitHub distribution, not a PyPI release. It requires Python 3.13 and the exact numerical dependency versions in pyproject.toml.

The paper's application data, simulation scripts, generated results and manuscript are not included in this repository. The original providers and research-verification route are described under data and reproducibility. No benchmark or general performance guarantee is implied by this showcase.

docs.title: From software to research
docs.text: The citation and credit page records authorship and code provenance. Publication details will be added when verified; no journal DOI is asserted here. Return to the author's software catalogue to explore related R and Python packages.

The inspected public source provides the installable estimator API, pinned Python 3.13 numerical dependencies, citation/provenance metadata and a small installation smoke test.

This documentation candidate adds navigation, installation guidance, a curated API overview, data-source boundaries and citation links. It does not change the estimator implementation or imply a new software release.

docs.title: Cite the software
docs.text:
Use the repository's CITATION.cff and record version 0.1.0 and the exact source revision used.

Mohammad Arashi and Bahadır Yüzbaşı. Shape-adaptive robust regression. Python software, version 0.1.0.

The associated manuscript is From Residual-Moment Penalties to Shape-Adaptive Robust Estimation under Skewness and Heavy Tails. Cite its verified publication record when available; no journal, DOI or acceptance claim is invented here.

docs.title: Preserve implementation credit
docs.text:
The Data Science Laboratory (DSLab) at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad (FUM) contributed to writing the initial Python implementation under Mohammad Arashi's supervision. Bahadır Yüzbaşı subsequently developed and validated the code used for the reported analyses.

See the code provenance statement. The estimator implementation is the unchanged validated v4 study module.

docs.title: License and feedback
docs.text: The source is GPL-3.0-or-later; see the license. Cite original data providers separately. Report a documentation issue through GitHub with a small synthetic example and environment details, not private datasets.

docs.title: Install in an isolated Python 3.13 environment
docs.text:
python3.13 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install 'shape-adaptive-robust-regression @ git+https://github.com/byuzbasi/shape-adaptive-robust-regression.git'

The distribution name uses hyphens; the import name uses underscores. The numerical requirements are NumPy 2.2.6, Numba 0.61.2 and SciPy 1.16.3. These versions are recorded in the package, rather than substituted by the documentation environment. No PyPI installation is claimed.

docs.title: A small interface demonstration
docs.text:
This is the README's artificial 40-observation, three-predictor example. It checks how to fit and predict; it is not a study of statistical performance.

import numpy as np
from shape_adaptive_robust_regression import ShapeAdaptiveEN

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
X = rng.normal(size=(40, 3))
y = 1 + X[:, 0] + rng.standard_t(3, size=40)
model = ShapeAdaptiveEN(n_iter=1, n_lam=3, k=3, seed=42).fit(X, y)
predictions = model.predict(X[:2])
print(predictions)

X is an observations-by-predictors numeric matrix; y is a matching numeric response vector. predict() returns one value per new row, using the fitted coefficients and intercept on the original response scale.

The deliberately small n_iter, n_lam and k are demonstration settings, not recommendations for an empirical analysis. A training-data CV choice does not replace held-out predictive evaluation.

docs.title: Inspect numerical information
docs.text:
from shape_adaptive_robust_regression import diagnostic_summary
print(diagnostic_summary(model))

Iteration-cap and KKT summaries describe numerical behavior; they do not prove predictive superiority. Keep a record of your call, seed and package versions. For the exact installation smoke test, see tests/test_install.py.

docs.title: API guide
docs.text: The public namespace is shape_adaptive_robust_regression. The table below is a curated entry point; the estimator source contains the exact signatures and implementation docstrings.

docs.title: Primary estimator
docs.text:
ShapeAdaptiveEN(alpha=0.5, c_grid=(1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0),
                n_iter=2, n_lam=15, k=5, seed=0,
                pilot=None, kkt_tol=None)

Starts from a pilot, estimates a bounded score from standardized pilot residuals, and fits an elastic net to the resulting pseudo-responses. alpha controls elastic-net mixing; c_grid contains score-shape candidates; n_iter is the number of updates; n_lam is the penalty-path size and k the CV fold count. seed controls the reproducible fold construction. pilot optionally supplies the initial fit. kkt_tol adds a final-target numerical bound when set. Defaults are documented, not changed by this site.

docs.title: Shape-penalized estimator
docs.text:
ShapePenalizedEN(lam=0.1, alpha=0.5, lam1=0.0, lam2=0.0,
                 robust=False, c_huber=1.345, c_clip=2.5,
                 scale=None, max_sweeps=1000, tol=1e-9,
                 beta_init=None, eps=1e-6, kkt_tol=None)

lam and alpha set elastic-net regularization. lam1 and lam2 weight residual skewness and excess-kurtosis penalties. robust=False uses least squares and raw centered residual moments; robust=True uses Huber loss and clipped standardized residual moments. c_huber, c_clip and scale govern that robust configuration. Solver controls are max_sweeps, tol, beta_init, eps and kkt_tol.

Both main classes expose fit(X, y), predict(X), coef_ and intercept_. Keep training and evaluation observations separate.

docs.title: Comparison and tuning interfaces
docs.text:
Object Role QuantileLasso(lam=0.01, taus=(0.5,)) LAD Lasso at the median or composite quantile regression Lasso fit_en_cv Elastic net, or Huber elastic net, selected by internal CV fit_sken_cv CV selection of residual-shape weights at the supplied penalty level fit_quantile_lasso_cv CV selection for the quantile-Lasso comparator diagnostic_summary(model) Compact refit/CV KKT and iteration-cap summaries

Consult the source docstrings for full helper signatures and returned diagnostic fields. LP-based quantile fits fail explicitly on optimizer failure and do not expose the coordinate-descent KKT diagnostic.

docs.title: Input dictionary
docs.text:
Input Interpretation X Numeric two-dimensional array: observations in rows, predictors in columns y Numeric response vector matching the rows of X New X Same predictor columns and order as training seed Fold-construction seed in the relevant CV helper/estimator

docs.title: Data sources and access
docs.text:
The repository contains no application datasets. The study cites these original providers; using the software does not transfer ownership of their data.

The paper reports the analysis protocols. Application workflows and study materials can be requested from the authors for research verification. This site does not claim that installing the package reproduces all paper results.

docs.title: Reproducible installation check
docs.text:
From a reviewed checkout and a Python 3.13 environment with the package installed:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m pip freeze

The existing test uses a small synthetic sample and checks finite predictions for the two principal classes. Record the source revision, Python version, dependency versions, configuration and seeds with any analysis. Neither this test nor a successful site build validates a production simulation study.

docs.title: Documentation environment
docs.text:
Documentation uses MkDocs/Material and a separate requirements-docs.txt. It does not import the estimator or execute fitting during site generation.

python3.13 -m venv .venv-docs
. .venv-docs/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs build --strict

The output is static HTML. Publication is a separate maintainer action.
